utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The first matter I want to deal with is the motion which was argued yesterday to exclude evidence obtained as a result of the execution of a search warrant. The Trial Chamber has now had the opportunity for considering the motion and the result is that the motion will be rejected and the evidence will be admitted. Written reasons for this decision will follow in due course. Two housekeeping matters. We shall not be sitting next Wednesday afternoon as some members of the court have to attend another hearing, but there is a possibility, which I wanted to raise with the parties, of sitting this Thursday morning. It's not on the calendar, but it happens that the hearing which I shall be attending early in the morning is, in fact, going to go fairly short, and it's possible that we could sit here at half past ten, if that is possible as far as the parties are concerned and, of course, the court organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I would hope that we would have concluded the examination of this witness in today's and tomorrow's sessions. If not, then Thursday might be a very, very valuable period of time to have available for him. I think it's highly unlikely that I could find another witness for the Thursday morning period which you've indicated or indeed that the period could be usefully used for a witness. There is one outstanding witness, one witness whose cross-examination is outstanding, but I don't think his cross-examination would be accomplished within a couple of hours. When this witness is concluded or at the end of the hearings this week, in any event, I've got a short application to make in respect of witnesses we seek to add to the list, and there are a few more things I want to say about procedural matters, probably ten minutes, but sometimes these ten minutes can grow. I know that although they've already spoken once, Mr. Naumovski indicated that he wanted another half an hour to come back on procedural matters. So, again, the Thursday might be a period of time that could be usefully used for procedural matters if we haven't finished them tomorrow afternoon, but I think for a witness, unlikely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: They are matters that should be resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: They have been hanging over for some time. Very well. I'll have inquiries made as to whether we could sit at half past ten on Thursday. Yes. I haven't raised it with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, there was a reference made by Mr. Smith yesterday to a letter authored by the Ministry of Defence, Mr. Jelavic, which Mr. Nice kindly provided to us yesterday. We don't have sufficient copies for the Trial Chamber to consider, but I've had copies made and it will be convenient and I'll distribute those now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. If you'd like to hand that in. As far as Thursday's hearing is concerned, if there is one, are the Defence available if necessary on Thursday morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The Kordic Defence would be, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We are okay, Your Honour. No problem with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If there are no other matters in open session we'll go into closed session.
